newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan sees Eurobond issue in Sept or Oct.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan sees Eurobond issue in Sept or Oct.

text.p: Kazakhstan will issue in September or October a $250-350 million Eurobond with a five or seven year maturity, the chief treasurer at the ex-Soviet state's Finance Ministry said on Tuesday.

"In September or October, Kazakhstan will issue dollar denominated Eurobonds for a total of $250-350 million," Daniyar Abulgazin told Reuters. "The maturity is likely to be five or seven years with concrete terms to be established in line with market conditions."

Last December, the Central Asian state tapped international markets with its debut $200-million Eurobond, which investors snapped up. The three-year bond, organised by Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, was priced to yield 9.3 percent, or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. treasury notes.

"The ministry hopes to use to its advantage the situation on international markets, which is characterised by permanently strong demand for bonds of countries with economies in transition," the Finance Ministry said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

The statement said the Kazakh economy was showing real growth for the second year in a row, adding that after five years of severe economic crisis, gross domestic product grew by 1.1 percent last year would keep growing this year.

"By offering its bonds, Kazakhstan plans to improve the liquidity of its securities on international markets...and to receive funds to support the reform of the national pension scheme," the statement said. The government has pledged to pay off pension debts of $480 million by the end of the year.

Last year international rating agencies Moody's and IBCA granted Kazakhstan a sovereign credit rating Ba3, while Standard and Poor's BB-, and the government has said the current ratings could be improved by the date of the new Eurobond issue.
